\[
xyz = 3,
\]
\[
(x-y)(y-z)(z-x) = 4,
\]
\[
(x+y)(y+z)(z+x) = 40.
\]

Compute the minimum possible value for \( x \).

Give the minimum value of x as an exact expression using only integers, rational numbers, and radicals (no trigonometric or inverse trigonometric functions, and no approximations).

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let

\[
a=\frac{x}{y},\qquad b=\frac{y}{z},\qquad c=\frac{z}{x}.
\]

Since \(x,y,z>0\), we have \(a,b,c>0\) and

\[
abc=1.
\]

Also,

\[
x+y=y(a+1),\qquad y+z=z(b+1),\qquad z+x=x(c+1),
\]

so

\[
(x+y)(y+z)(z+x)=xyz(a+1)(b+1)(c+1).
\]

Using \(xyz=3\), this gives

\[
3(a+1)(b+1)(c+1)=40
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(a+1)(b+1)(c+1)=\frac{40}{3}.
\]

Similarly,

\[
x-y=y(a-1),\qquad y-z=z(b-1),\qquad z-x=x(c-1),
\]

so

\[
(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)=xyz(a-1)(b-1)(c-1),
\]

hence

\[
3(a-1)(b-1)(c-1)=4
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(a-1)(b-1)(c-1)=\frac{4}{3}.
\]

Now let

\[
S=a+b+c,\qquad P=ab+bc+ca.
\]

Because \(abc=1\),

\[
(a+1)(b+1)(c+1)=S+P+2,
\]

and

\[
(a-1)(b-1)(c-1)=S-P.
\]

Thus

\[
S+P+2=\frac{40}{3}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad S+P=\frac{34}{3},
\]

and

\[
S-P=\frac{4}{3}.
\]

Solving,

\[
S=\frac{19}{3},\qquad P=5.
\]

Therefore \(a,b,c\) are the roots of

\[
t^3-S t^2+P t-1=0,
\]

so

\[
t^3-\frac{19}{3}t^2+5t-1=0.
\]

Multiplying by \(3\),

\[
3t^3-19t^2+15t-3=0.
\]

This factors as

\[
(3t-1)(t^2-6t+3)=0,
\]

so the roots are

\[
\frac13,\qquad 3-\sqrt6,\qquad 3+\sqrt6.
\]

Hence

\[
\{a,b,c\}=\left\{\frac13,\,3-\sqrt6,\,3+\sqrt6\right\}.
\]

Now \(a=x/y\) and \(c=z/x\), so

\[
y=\frac{x}{a},\qquad z=cx.
\]

Using \(xyz=3\),

\[
x\cdot \frac{x}{a}\cdot cx=3
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
x^3=\frac{3a}{c}.
\]

Thus possible values of \(x^3\) are obtained by taking \(3a/c\), where \(a\) and \(c\) are two distinct elements of

\[
\left\{\frac13,\,3-\sqrt6,\,3+\sqrt6\right\}.
\]

Since all three are positive, the smallest possible value of \(x^3\) is obtained by choosing the smallest numerator and the largest denominator:

\[
a=\frac13,\qquad c=3+\sqrt6.
\]

Therefore

\[
x_{\min}^3
=
3\cdot \frac{\frac13}{3+\sqrt6}
=
\frac{1}{3+\sqrt6}
=
\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}.
\]

This value is achieved by taking

\[
x=\sqrt[3]{\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}},\qquad
y=3x,\qquad
z=(3+\sqrt6)x.
\]

Hence the minimum possible value of \(x\) is

\[
\boxed{\sqrt[3]{\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}}}.
\]
